Maya (PM): Quick sync — we got a direct ask from AtlasHealth for stronger DP prioritization: they want a private-preview that supports per-route throttles, audit logs, and a rollback SLA. Can we map this to our priority buckets and decide what we can commit to for beta?
Rob (Eng Lead): Short answer: per-route throttles + audit logs are doable for private within 6 weeks if we scope throttles to token-rate and concurrent sessions. Rollback SLA needs infra work — depends if they need cross-region failover.
Tess (Design): Do we need any UX for the throttles? Atlas expects a UI knob and an API. We should at least provide a minimal console flow and example curl snippets.
Devon (Customer Success): Atlas steering committee will sign up only if we promise a clear launch criteria doc and an escalation path. They also want a sampling of model outputs for compliance.
Sasha (Research): We can put together a small eval harness for their prompts (50 prompts) and an automatic quality regression check. I can own that.
Maya (PM): Good — let's break into must-have/minimum vs nice-to-have. My proposal: MUST = per-route throttles (tokens/concurrency), audit logs (structured events), acceptance tests (eval harness + 50 prompts), launch criteria doc. NICE = console UI, cross-region rollback SLA, managed sampling pipeline. Thoughts?
Rob (Eng Lead): That seems reasonable. Note: audit logs require schema decisions (what fields) and retention defaults. Will need SRE input for retention and HSM/KMS hook for Private. Estimate: must-have 6w, nice-to-have +4w.
Tess (Design): For MVP console, we can reuse the existing route config panel — add a "throttle" section with dropdowns and a small help tooltip. I can mock this in 3 days.
Devon (Customer Success): Can we make the launch criteria explicit? Suggestion: 1) Eval harness passes (no regression > x% on their 50 prompts), 2) Load test: sustained 200 rps at 300ms P95 on dedicated config, 3) Audit logs contain token-level attribution + request metadata.
Maya (PM): Agree. Put those in the doc. Also add "support window": 2-week onboarding with daily check-ins. Atlas wants a rollback SLA though — can we offer an "operational rollback" commitment (manual rollback within 2 hours) instead of automated cross-region?
Rob (Eng Lead): We can commit to manual rollback within 2 hours for the beta (runbook + on-call escalation). Automated cross-region failover we'd table for GA.
Sasha (Research): I'll draft the eval harness and share an exporter that emits the sample outputs to a secure bucket for Atlas review. Needs an agreed-upon NDA clause — Devon to confirm.
Devon (Customer Success): I'll confirm NDA and negotiate the sampling cadence. Also ask Atlas if they can provide a priority prompt set — speeds up eval.
Maya (PM): Action items: Rob -> tech spec for throttles + audit log schema by next Tue; Tess -> console mock by Thu; Sasha -> eval harness draft by Fri; Devon -> legal/NDA + Atlas prompt set by Fri. I'll assemble the launch criteria doc and share a rolling timeline.
Rob (Eng Lead): One more thing — capacity. If Atlas runs heavy, we need an autoscale policy for dedicated pools. I'll include recommended commit levels and burst config in the spec.
Tess (Design): UX note: make default throttle conservative. We can add a tooltip: "Start conservative, increase after onboarding."
ops-bot: Reminder — Maya scheduled a "DP scope negotiation" meeting on 2025-07-08 10:00 AM in #product. (meeting-link)
Maya (PM): Thanks all. If no objections, I'll send the spec template and start the stakeholder invite list. :thumbsup:
Devon (Customer Success): No objections from me. I'll loop in Atlas PM and legal after NDA check.
Rob (Eng Lead): 👍 will start a draft PR in eng-repo and assign reviewers.
Sasha (Research): Will tag the eval artifacts so we can trace regressions.
Maya (PM): Great — closing thread for now. I'll post the doc link when ready.
